newsitem.title: INDIA: U.S. balloonist plans to land in India.
newsitem.headline: U.S. balloonist plans to land in India.

text.p: A U.S. balloonist planned to land in India on Monday, cutting short his solo attempt to fly around the world after six days in the air, his support team said.
Steve Fossett was expected to set down in Varanasi, India, halfway between Calcutta and Delhi, at about 0619 GMT, a spokesman for the support team in Chicago told Reuters by telephone.

The spokesman said Fossett, who took off from Busch Stadium in St Louis on January 13, expected to break the six-day, 16-minute endurance record for a balloon flight and then set down near Varanasi in the northern state of Uttar Pradesh.
Varanasi is one of the Hindu religion's holiest cities, known for its bathing "ghats", or steps, which descend into the Ganges River.
On Friday, the commodity broker-turned-adventurer broke his own record for balloon distance travel when he passed 8,747 km (5,435 miles) over Algeria.
But political problems over the use of Libyan air space cost Fossett the around-the-world bid when he was forced to burn extra fuel to change his route, putting him in a slower wind pattern.
